description: We’re a team of curious builders who love turning complex space data into something anyone can explore. For Space Apps 2026, we’re building an interactive CLPS Lunar Mission Browser that maps landing sites, shows what each mission carried, and recreates the sky as seen from the Moon’s surface. Our goal is to make NASA’s return to the Moon easy and engaging for everyone to follow.

details:
LunaView

What does your project do and how does it work?

LunaView is an interactive web application designed to make lunar exploration easier. Users can explore the Moon through an interactive LROC map, select locations, search for places, enter coordinates and choose observation times using UTC, Julian Day or Modified Julian Day. The application provides an orbit view with Sun and Earth markers, field of view controls and a search feature for celestial objects. It also provides site reports containing information about sunlight, surface temperature, radiation, Earth visibility and ground conditions.

LunaView also includes a rover mission simulator where users can select different rover configurations, plan routes using waypoints, view elevation profiles and identify potential terrain hazards.

What benefits does it have?

LunaView brings several lunar exploration features into one application. It makes lunar location information easier to access and understand without requiring users to navigate multiple specialised tools. It supports flexible location and time selection, provides environmental information through site reports and allows users to experiment with rover route planning. It can also help students, educators and space enthusiasts learn about lunar exploration.

What is the intended impact of the project?

Our aim is to make lunar exploration more accessible and simplify the initial process of exploring potential lunar locations. LunaView can help students and space enthusiasts understand how location, time, sunlight and Earth visibility influence lunar conditions. It also provides a foundation for future mission planning by bringing location exploration, celestial viewing and rover route planning together.

What tools, coding languages, hardware or software did you use?

LunaView was developed as a browser-based web application. It uses NASA's Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter Camera (LROC) lunar map for surface exploration. The application includes interactive mapping, astronomical visualisation, time controls, site reports and a rover simulator. NASA LOLA terrain integration is also planned as part of future development.

How is your project creative?

LunaView combines lunar location exploration, Sun and Earth visualisation, environmental site reports and rover route planning in one application. Instead of providing only a lunar map, it allows users to interact with different locations, explore celestial viewing information and experiment with rover routes. This makes the application useful for both learning and lunar exploration.

What factors did your team consider?

We have considered accessibility, ease of use, location selection, observation time, scientific information and terrain conditions while developing LunaView. We wanted the application to be understandable for users without specialist knowledge while still providing useful information about lunar exploration. We also considered the importance of reliable data, accurate celestial positioning and potential surface hazards. Future development will focus on terrain-based horizon calculations, sunlight and communication window predictions, and comparisons between different landing sites and dates.
